title.en: The Three Things That Do Not Decay

year_display.en: The conversation 549 BCE; the Zuo Zhuan compiled c. 4th century BCE
year_display.zh: 事在公元前 549 年；《左传》约成书于公元前 4 世纪

edition.en: Zuo Zhuan, Duke Xiang, year 24, as given on Chinese Wikisource; modern punctuation added by Cold Library, characters unchanged.
edition.zh: 《左传·襄公二十四年》，据维基文库；标点为冷冻图书馆所加，文字未改。

basis.en: From the Zuo Zhuan, compiled in the fourth century BCE.
basis.zh: 出自《左传》，约成书于公元前四世纪。

note.en: A short exchange from the Zuo Zhuan: the chief minister of Jin boasts that his family's long line of offices is what 'not decaying' means, and the envoy from Lu politely disagrees. His answer, virtue first, then deeds, then words, became the classical Chinese account of what outlasts a person. Notice that a library lives on the third rung, and that the example he gives is a man whose sayings were still quoted after he was gone.
note.zh: 《左传》中一段简短的对话：晋国执政范宣子夸耀自家世代相承的官位，认为这就是“不朽”；鲁国使者穆叔委婉地表示不同意。他的回答——先立德，次立功，再立言——成了中国古典中关于什么能比人更长久的经典说法。留意图书馆正住在第三级上，而穆叔举的例子，是一个人去世之后，他说过的话仍被人援引。

excerpt.orig: 大上有立德，其次有立功，其次有立言。
excerpt.en: Highest is to establish virtue; next, to establish deeds; next, to establish words.
excerpt.zh: 大上有立德，其次有立功，其次有立言。

gloss.en: The twenty-fourth year of Duke Xiang of Lu, 549 BCE. The Zuo Zhuan dates events by the reign years of the rulers of Lu.
gloss.zh: 鲁襄公二十四年，即公元前 549 年。《左传》按鲁国国君在位的年数纪年。

gloss.en: Shusun Bao, a minister of Lu; Mu is his posthumous name. In his reply he calls himself Bao (豹), by his personal name, as courtesy required.
gloss.zh: 叔孙豹，鲁国大夫，“穆”是谥号。答话中他自称“豹”，以名自称，表示谦敬。

gloss.en: 如: to go to. Jin was then the leading state of the alliance of the central states.
gloss.zh: 如：往，到……去。晋是当时诸侯盟会的盟主国。

gloss.en: Shi Gai, chief minister of Jin, of the Fan lineage; Xuan is his posthumous name. Below he calls himself Gai (匄), by his personal name.
gloss.zh: 士匄，晋国执政的正卿，属范氏，“宣”是谥号。下文的“匄”是他以名自称。

gloss.en: 逆: to go out and meet, to receive a guest.
The clan of the sage king Yao; 虞 is the age of Shun, who came after him. Fan Xuanzi traces his line back to Yao and then names the clan it bore under each dynasty: Xia, Shang and Zhou.
gloss.zh: 唐尧的氏号；虞指虞舜的时代。范宣子把自家世系上溯到尧，再一一列举它在夏、商、周各代的氏号。

gloss.en: 'Dragon-tamers'. The Zuo Zhuan tells elsewhere (Duke Zhao, year 29) how Liu Lei, a descendant of Yao, learned to rear dragons and served the Xia king Kongjia, who gave him this clan name.
gloss.zh: 据《左传·昭公二十九年》，陶唐氏的后人刘累学会驯养龙，事奉夏王孔甲，被赐氏为御龙氏。

gloss.en: 夏 here means the Xia, the central states of the Zhou world. Jin presided over their covenant, and the family took the name Fan from its fief in Jin.
gloss.zh: 夏：诸夏，指中原各诸侯国。晋国主持诸侯的盟会；范氏得名于这一家在晋国的封邑范。

gloss.en: Hereditary emolument: office and income passed down a family. This is what Mushu sets against 'not decaying'.
gloss.zh: 世代承袭的官位与俸禄。穆叔正是拿它与“不朽”相对照。

gloss.en: Zang Sunchen (d. 617 BCE), a minister of Lu remembered for his sayings, which were still being quoted generations after his death.
gloss.zh: 臧孙辰（？—前 617），鲁国大夫，以言论著称，去世多年后他的话仍被人援引。

gloss.en: 大 is read as 太: 太上, highest of all.
To keep one's surname and receive a lineage name. The surname (姓) marked a family's ancient descent; the lineage name (氏) came from a fief or an office.
gloss.zh: 保住姓，承受氏。古时姓表示族源，氏多由封地或官职而来。

gloss.en: The ancestral temple; 祊 is a sacrifice offered at the temple gate, and stands for the temple itself.
gloss.zh: 宗庙。祊，在宗庙门内举行的祭祀，借指宗庙。
